clue.text: Vehicle that has been booked?

parts.note: a van loaded with books for lending, playing on 'booked' meaning reserved

explanation.surface: A question about a taxi or coach that someone has reserved in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling van stocked with lending books is a vehicle filled with books, hence 'booked'.

clue.text: You can't get out if these aren't kept open

definitions.text: You can't get out if these aren't kept open

parts.words: You can't get out if these aren't kept open
parts.note: reads like doors or exits, but means choices you leave available so that a way out remains

explanation.surface: A warning that exits must stay unlocked or you will be trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping choices open is the idiom; with none left open there is no escape route.

clue.text: Bird is injected with thiamine

indicators.note: the word 'is' receives a shot of something, so other letters go inside it

parts.note: thiamine is vitamin B1, written here as B and I (the figure 1 read as the letter I)

explanation.surface: A bird is given a vitamin jab by a vet.
explanation.walkthrough: Thiamine is vitamin B1, and here the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred wading bird of ancient Egypt, with a long curved bill.

clue.text: They've got on in life

parts.note: sounds like successful people, but 'got on' here means grown old

explanation.surface: A remark about people who have prospered in their careers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'getting on' is an idiom for ageing, so old people are those well on in years.

clue.text: One politician confronts every single charge

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP, Member of Parliament
every single one means each

explanation.surface: A lone MP faces down every accusation thrown at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confronts' only sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To accuse formally, especially of an offence in public office.

clue.text: It's unusual to retire in Tipperary

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the run is read backwards
the letters wanted sit inside the place name Tipperary

parts.note: a run of letters inside this word

explanation.surface: Someone thinks moving to an Irish county in old age would be odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to ERAR inside TippERARy; 'to retire' turns it backwards. Tipperary is a county in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom met with is scarce or uncommon.

clue.text: Stalks out of the kitchen-garden

parts.note: reads as someone storming off from the vegetable patch, but means plant stems grown there

explanation.surface: Someone angrily marches out of the vegetable plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Its pink edible stems are a staple crop of the home vegetable plot.

clue.text: What a person who in, trades in a row does?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'What a person who in, trades in a row does?' has lost a word after 'who' (probably 'butts' or similar); no source found to restore it.
annotationWithheld.clue: What a person who in, trades in a row does?

clue.text: They are held up by the neck

definitions.text: They are held up by the neck

parts.words: They are held up by the neck
parts.note: suggests something hanged, but means a necklace hanging round the throat

explanation.surface: A grim line about things suspended by the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace of threaded beads hangs from and is supported by the wearer's neck.

clue.text: Unheard and untested

definitions.meaning: of a court case, not yet heard by judges
never put to the test or tried out

explanation.definitionFit: A case not yet heard in court has not come to trial; something never tested has not been tried.

clue.text: Job seeking

definitions.meaning: an occupation or pastime one follows
the act of chasing after something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hobby or occupation and the act of chasing.

clue.text: Opening for a machine operator

parts.note: sounds like a job vacancy, but means the gap where a coin is put into a vending machine

explanation.surface: A job advert for someone to run factory machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow aperture into which coins are pushed to work a machine.

clue.text: Start playing snooker, getting a series of points

definitions.meaning: the opening shot of a frame of snooker scatters the reds
a run of consecutive pots scoring points in one visit

explanation.definitionFit: In snooker the opening shot and a scoring run at the table share one name.

clue.text: Dial out from Salvador

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word dial are put out of order

explanation.surface: Telephoning out of a Latin American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salvador' looks like the city or country; it is the painter's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador is the first name of the Spanish surrealist painter.

clue.text: Maturing alcoholic drink in silver container

indicators.note: the silver is a container holding the drink, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Spirit being matured in a silver vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver container' puts GIN inside AG, the chemical symbol for silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older or ripening over time, as wine or cheese does.

clue.text: Go quietly to spill the beans

definitions.meaning: to tell tales, inform on someone

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both creeping about unseen and telling tales to authority.

clue.text: Organ bright with flowers

parts.note: the nose is an organ of smell
gay in its older sense of bright and cheerful

explanation.surface: A church organ decked out cheerfully with blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A small posy or bunch of blooms.

clue.text: Many women have this combination of give and take

parts.note: to hand something over is to give it
to bag is to take or seize

explanation.surface: A neat phrase about the compromise most women manage in relationships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combination of' just joins the two verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag carried by women to hold purses and keys.

clue.text: Dependable way to limit bloodshed

definitions.meaning: to stop the flow of blood from a wound

explanation.definitionFit: As adjective it means loyal; as verb it means stopping blood flowing from a wound.

clue.text: A crime upsets a whole continent

indicators.note: upsetting throws the letters of these words into disorder

explanation.surface: A crime causes outrage across an entire continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsets' rearranges ACRIME into AMERIC; the second 'a' then goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Americas form a landmass spanning north and south.

clue.text: School principal to order a hearing-aid

parts.note: the head teacher of a school
to set is to arrange or put in order

explanation.surface: The headmaster has to order a hearing device.
explanation.definitionFit: Earphones with a microphone, worn to help one hear.

clue.text: Cockney thief may end up in hot water

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang, 'leaf' rhymes with thief

definitions.text: may end up in hot water
definitions.meaning: loose tea leaves are steeped in boiling water in the pot

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang is the working-class London habit of replacing a word with a phrase that rhymes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for a robber, and also a fragment of tea brewed in a teapot.

clue.text: Capital cover for Roman soldiers

parts.note: suggests a shelter in the capital city, but 'capital' means head: a roof of shields over legionaries' heads

explanation.surface: Shelter provided in Rome for the army.
explanation.definitionFit: The tortoise formation, where legionaries locked shields overhead as protection.

clue.text: It receives word of a murder plot

indicators.note: the letters of the words are plotted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone hears news of a planned killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a conspiracy but is the anagram signal for A MURDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane in the ear vibrates when sound, including speech, reaches it.

clue.text: The top copy required and ten more

parts.note: to ape is to copy
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: An office instruction for a top copy plus ten duplicates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Required and' and 'more' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: It's the minister's place to designate names

indicators.note: read as de-sign-ate, the word names loses its existing order

explanation.surface: A clergyman claims the right to name things.
explanation.definitionFit: The house provided for a Presbyterian or Scottish clergyman.

clue.text: Deliver without charge

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to liberate and costing nothing.

clue.text: East European not quite in bondage

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a person in bondage is a slave

explanation.surface: An Eastern European almost enslaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the final E of SLAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a people of Eastern Europe such as Poles, Czechs and Russians.

clue.text: How about a call to slow down!

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of the word go out of order

explanation.surface: A rider asking how to call on a horse to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' rearranges HOW into WHO, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The command used to halt or slow a horse.

clue.text: They're frozen in suspense

parts.note: suggests people too tense to move, but means ice hanging down from eaves

explanation.surface: Onlookers too anxious to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging spikes of ice are literally suspended, frozen drips.

clue.text: Crafty ruse he'd introduced

indicators.note: something crafty is cunningly worked, signalling the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cunning trick that someone brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone in or bring them to a seat is to usher them.

clue.text: Host ministering to the needy

parts.note: a host is an army; this one is a Christian charity organised on military lines

explanation.surface: A party host serving food to poor guests.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian church organised with military ranks, famed for charity work.
